description: FIRST MIRROR-OF-A-HOLED-PLATE GOLDEN (FINDINGS #2 — mirroring a plate with a hole about its midplane silently ERASED the hole: the mirror reflected the whole FILLED body and boolean-UNIONED the reflection, so the reflected solid material filled the original hole and the result was the featureless brick. The #1 mirror use case destroyed exactly what it mirrored). A 40 x 40 mm plate sketched on the XY datum, extruded 20 mm into the box [0,40] x [0,40] x [0,20]; a SINGLE r4 through-hole drilled by the HOLE FEATURE at (10,20) on the +Z face; a YZ-parallel offset datum at x=20 (the plate's x-midplane); then a MIRROR about that datum. Because the immediately-preceding body-affecting feature is a Hole, the mirror reflects THAT hole's removal tool about the plane and REMOVES it (FINDINGS #2 fix, the same cut-awareness the pattern uses): the seed hole at x=10 stays and its reflection at x=30 is cut, so the plate ends with a hole on BOTH sides of the midplane -- NOT the whole-body reflect-and-union that would fill the hole to a solid brick. A five-feature TREE (sketch -> extrude add -> hole -> datum -> mirror) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as every other golden. Locks: the mirror cut-source inference over a Hole (prev_body_feature is a HoleFeature -> state.last_hole_tools), mirror_cut's reflected-tool placement + variadic body.cut + lump-count-preserving finalize, the offset-datum plane resolved through the sketch-plane funnel, GProp over the drilled plate, exact topology after clean(), and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte-determinism and STEP round-trip. The reflect-and-union mirror path (a body clearing the plane -> disjoint 2V) is UNCHANGED and regression-guarded by mirror-triangle-prism-2x.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Plate: outer square x,y in [0,40] on XY (4 lines, no constraints -> zero residual, planegcs returns input positions bitwise), extruded 20 mm along +Z = the box [0,40] x [0,40] x [0,20], volume 40*40*20 = 32000 mm^3.

seed hole: the HOLE feature drills a diameter-8 (r4) through-all bore at (10,20) on the +Z face (outward normal +Z). The drill cuts INTO the solid along -Z, removing exactly pi*4^2*20 per hole. The hole is strictly interior (x=10 > r4, y=20 centred) so it does not touch the plate boundary.
mirror plane: a datum parallel to the YZ origin plane (normal +X), slid +20 mm along its normal -> the plane x=20, which is the plate's x-midplane (x in [0,40]).

mirror: the source feature is the Hole, so the mirror REFLECTS THAT HOLE'S removal tool about x=20 and cuts it: the seed hole at x=10 reflects to x=30 (both at y=20), so the plate ends with TWO disjoint r4 through-holes at x = 10 and x = 30. Each is fully interior and 20 mm apart (r4 each -> 12 mm clearance), so the plate stays ONE connected solid (a cut severing it would be mirror_failed).

volume = 32000 - 2 * (pi * 4^2) * 20 = 32000 - 640*pi = 29989.380701702532 mm^3 (two disjoint cylindrical through-holes removed, no overlap, so exactly 2x the single-hole removal). The whole-body-union bug would instead give 32000 (the hole filled) -- this value FAILS on the old behaviour.

surface_area = 2*(1600 - 2*pi*16)  [top + bottom plate caps, each pierced by both holes]  + 4*(40*20)  [four outer side walls]  + 2*(2*pi*4*20)  [two cylindrical hole walls]  = 2*1600 - 2*32*pi + 3200 + 2*160*pi = 3200 - 64*pi + 3200 + 320*pi = 6400 + 256*pi = 7204.247719318987 mm^2.

centroid = (20, 20, 10) mm by symmetry: the two hole centres x = 10, 30 are symmetric about the midplane x=20, both at y=20 (the plate's y-centre), and the holes run the full uniform 20 mm depth (z mid-height 10). A union bug (filled brick) would also centre at (20,20,10), so centroid alone does not discriminate -- the VOLUME does.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,40,20]: the holes are strictly interior, so the AABB is the un-drilled plate's box.

topology: 8 faces (top + bottom plate caps, 4 outer side walls, 2 cylindrical hole walls), 18 edges (top boundary = 4 rect edges + 2 hole circles = 6; bottom = 6; 4 vertical box corner edges; 1 vertical seam edge on each of the 2 periodic hole cylinders = 2), 1 shell -- the same structure as the two-hole plate golden (sketch-extrude-plate-2holes). The union bug would give a SOLID brick (6 faces, 12 edges, no cylinder walls), so this count also discriminates the fix.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default, isRelative=False): each full hole circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (radius 4 keeps linear deflection non-binding). Two periodic hole cylinders = 2 * ((126+1)*2 nodes, 126*2 tris) = 2 * (254, 252) = 508 vertices / 504 triangles. Each plate cap is a planar face with a 4-node rectangular outer loop + two 126-gon holes = 4 + 2*126 = 256 boundary nodes, triangulated with holes to 256 - 2 + 2*2 = 258 triangles (no interior node); two caps = 512 vertices / 516 triangles. Four rectangular side walls = 4 * (4 nodes, 2 tris) = 16 vertices / 8 triangles. Totals = 508 + 512 + 16 = 1036 vertices and 504 + 516 + 8 = 1028 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-CUT + REFLECTION tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The mirror reflection is an EXACT handedness-reversing isometry, but the reflected cylindrical tool is boolean-CUT through curved walls whose GProp volume/surface use Gauss quadrature, so a small residual compounds through the cut -- the same numerically heavier path as the rotating pattern-cut-6hole golden (documented 1e-8). Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-24, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs): volume |29989.380701702532 - 29989.380701702525| ~ 7.0e-12, surface_area ~ 1.1e-12, centroid.x/.y ~ 4e-15, centroid.z ~ 2e-15, AABB bounds exactly 0.0. Documented ceiling 1e-8 covers the worst measured residual (~7.0e-12, the volume) with ~1400x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform variation across CI hosts, matching the established curved-CUT posture of pattern-cut-6hole while staying 10x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 kernel bound. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
